name: Marta Temido, Adam Jarubas - Proposition de la Commission
title: REPORT on the proposal for a Directive of the European Parliament and of the Council amending Directives 2001/18/EC and 2010/53/EU as regards the placing on the market of genetically modified micro-organisms and the processing of organs
part_text:
Parliament wants two laws updated. One covers genetically modified micro-organisms — bacteria, fungi, viruses — used in products like fertilisers or waste treatment. It asks for a faster approval path for those with a long safety record, but keeps safety checks, monitoring and renewals. The other covers human organs prepared before transplant. It asks for authorisation of these techniques, ethical safeguards, data protection and better cross-border cooperation on organ sharing.

- Genetically modified microbes with a proven safety record could get faster EU approval, with monitoring still decided by national authorities.
- Organ processing before transplant would need national authorisation, with patient information and data protection rules.
- Parliament's position now goes to EU governments for negotiation; the text is not final law yet.
